/commands.from: Each tool has typed fields such as `url`, `selector`, `text`, `key`, `session`, and `allowedDomains`, so MCP clients show meaningful approval prompts instead of raw command arrays. The common `allowedDomains` array maps to `--allowed-domains` and activates the same WebRTC containment and launch-mode restrictions. The common `idleTimeout` string maps to `--idle-timeout`, accepts values such as `30s`, `5m`, `1h`, or raw milliseconds, and accepts `0` to disable idle shutdown. Each tool also accepts `extraArgs` for per-command options and display or emulation flags such as `--engine`; `extraArgs` cannot set `--config` or global flags that change network, file, policy, or host access. Set host-wide options in the MCP server's environment or selected config. Structured `allowedDomains` is rejected when the server already sets allowed domains. Tool discovery is paginated and includes read-only/open-world annotations so modern MCP clients can load the large typed surface incrementally.
/commands.to:
Each tool has typed fields such as `url`, `selector`, `text`, and `key`, so MCP clients show meaningful approval prompts instead of raw command arrays. Tool discovery is paginated and includes read-only/open-world annotations so modern MCP clients can load the large typed surface incrementally.

Every tool also accepts the shared arguments `session`, `restore`, `allowedDomains`, `extraArgs`, `timeoutMs`, `namespace`, `restoreSave`, `restoreCheckUrl`, `restoreCheckText`, `restoreCheckFn`, `caCert`, `useSystemCa`, `clearCaCert`, `idleTimeout`, and `relaunch`. A tool's schema lists only the ones that usually matter for it: `session` on every tool, `restore` and `relaunch` on `open` and `tab_new`, `allowedDomains` and `extraArgs` on `open`, `tab_new`, and `read`, and `timeoutMs` on tools that navigate, wait, or run scripts. The server's `initialize` instructions describe all of them. `allowedDomains` maps to `--allowed-domains`, activates the same WebRTC containment and launch-mode restrictions, and is rejected when the server already sets allowed domains. `idleTimeout` maps to `--idle-timeout`, accepts values such as `30s`, `5m`, `1h`, or raw milliseconds, and accepts `0` to disable idle shutdown. `relaunch: true` maps to `--relaunch`. `extraArgs` carries per-command options and display or emulation flags such as `--engine`; it cannot set `--config` or global flags that change network, file, policy, or host access. Set host-wide options in the MCP server's environment or selected config.

/files.from: `--allow-file-access` is Chromium-only. It allows `file://` pages to load and access other local files through browser APIs such as `fetch` and XHR.
/files.to:
With Chrome, `--allow-file-access` allows `file://` pages to load and access other local files through browser APIs such as `fetch` and XHR.

With Lightpanda, the default engine, `file://` pages open without the flag: agent-browser serves them from disk through a reserved host, and the page can load files from the folders the session opened (other paths return 403). `--allow-file-access` lifts that limit. A local `.pdf` relaunches the session with Chrome. See [Lightpanda local files](/engines/lightpanda#local-files).
